input_step: Control bytes are decoded by the adapter with new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true}); JSON.parse receives only that string. The UTF-8 step is the adapter's, not the parser's.
coverage: No parser source lines: JSON.parse is V8 C++ inside the node binary and V8 source-range coverage lists no JSON parser script (the run-control checks this). Feedback is gdb function-entry hits on v8::internal::JsonParser<...> text symbols of the pinned, unstripped node binary.
native_feedback_limit: The base control records one-shot JsonParser function-entry sets through gdb; that probe is not AFL++ feedback. A separate AFL++ overlay hashes these function names into its bitmap and requires SYS_PTRACE and seccomp=unconfined. Neither route measures parser source lines, basic blocks, or edges; inlined code is invisible. The probe image records Debian's gdb version but does not hash-pin its package.

source_feedback.runtime: Node.js 26.10.0 source-built from the official tarball (V8 14.6.202.34-node.34) with Clang 20.1.8
source_feedback.official_binary_link: bin/node in the signed linux-arm64 tarball has sha256 71b004f18a82f3ea8f26109798564a12e5e4c7989a4c35b93851830b5815dd03, the pinned binary of the base image; the source tarball is listed in the same signed SHASUMS256.
source_feedback.compiler: clang-20 1:20.1.8-2ubuntu8 (official linux-arm64 release builds use Clang 20.1)
source_feedback.instrumented_node_note: Two independent from-scratch Docker builds on 2026-11-17 produced this same node binary.

source_feedback_limit: Clang source-based line coverage of V8's JSON parser, measured on a Node.js 26.10.0 binary built from the official source tarball, not on the pinned official binary (whose hash differs because of the build and the instrumentation). Only deps/v8/src/json/json-parser.cc is instrumented; lines are reported for json-parser.cc and json-parser.h code compiled into that object. JSON.parse builtin glue, string internalization outside the parser, and the adapter's TextDecoder step are not counted. These are replay line counts, not AFL++ edges: the AFL++ overlay still uses the gdb function-entry bridge.
